objective: Determine whether a separately versioned historical USD baseline can be grounded in point-in-time on-chain ETH/USD evidence across the nine reviewed historical Sentry representatives without changing current R3 semantics.

calibration_surface_result.conclusion: EXECUTABLE_BASELINE_R1 USD calibration is genuinely non-portable across the reviewed historical representatives: early WETH/USDT0 infrastructure is absent, later WETH/USDT0 infrastructure is too shallow for the frozen $2/$5 notionals, and the sole full-calibration representative uses USDT0 as its launch base.

oracle_discovery.purpose: Test whether documented Ink mainnet ETH/USD push-style oracle candidates existed and exposed point-in-time data at each historical decision block. Current documentation is candidate provenance only, not proof of historical availability.
measurements: contract bytecode presence at decision block
description() at decision block when supported
version() at decision block when supported
updatedAt nonzero and not after decision-block timestamp

decision_rules: The completed calibration-surface discovery falsifies an adapter-only explanation for the historical compatibility failure; do not repair the adapter or shrink R1 notionals to manufacture coverage.
Oracle discovery is availability/evidence discovery only. Do not select a freshness threshold or a winning oracle based on observed prices in this gate.

A candidate is point-in-time structurally usable at a representative only if its contract has code at that block and latestRoundData returns a positive answer with nonzero updatedAt not later than the decision-block timestamp.

If no candidate is structurally usable across all WETH representatives, do not use retrospective off-chain prices to fill gaps; the next policy decision must consider a non-USD or explicitly partially observed historical evidence contract.

If one or more candidates are structurally usable across all WETH representatives, freeze a separately versioned historical calibration policy and freshness rule before testing historical baselines or running the 147-launch replay.
Do not use future prices, retrospective centralized-exchange prices, outcome-conditioned sizing, or per-token adaptive notionals.
prohibitions: Do not change current R3 baseline semantics or authority.
Do not modify the five frozen EXECUTABLE_BASELINE_R1 notionals.
Do not choose an oracle freshness threshold in the oracle-availability discovery gate.
Do not use current oracle documentation as proof of historical availability.
Do not authorize or run the full 147-launch replay.
Do not add signing, approvals, swap construction, transaction broadcast, private keys, or execution authority.
Do not use future or retrospective off-chain prices as point-in-time evidence.
Do not merge without explicit user authority.
notes: The user explicitly authorized HISTORICAL_BASELINE_POLICY_R1 after HISTORICAL_COMPATIBILITY_R1 stopped on frozen baseline semantics.
Stage A calibration-surface discovery completed without changing R3 or the frozen R1 notionals and established genuine historical non-portability.
Stage B is limited to read-only point-in-time oracle availability discovery. It does not self-authorize a historical policy, replay, FAST_VET, canary, merge, signing, or execution.
